questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has digitized all his patient files. Dr. Tazi keeps his files in paper format. According to Article 12 of Law 09-08, what is their respective obligation towards the CNDP?
options: Only Dr. Chamssi must declare personal data processing
Neither has any obligation because health data is excluded
Both must declare their processing, regardless of the medium
Only Dr. Tazi must declare because paper is more risky
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Law 09-08 applies to any processing of personal data, regardless of the medium. We both must declare.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will help you with your declaration.'

questions.question: Dr. Tazi never made a CNDP declaration for his paper files. Dr. Chamssi informs him of the risks. According to Article 52 of Law 09-08, what fine is he exposed to?
options: No fine, paper files are excluded
A fine of 1,000 to 5,000 DH
A fine of 10,000 to 100,000 DH
A fine of 100,000 to 500,000 DH
questions.explanation: Dr. Chamssi explains: 'Article 52 provides for a fine of 10,000 to 100,000 DH for failure to make a prior declaration.' Dr. Tazi: 'I will regularize my situation immediately.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has integrated the CNDP receipt number into his forms. Dr. Tazi simply displays a notice in the waiting room. Dr. Chamssi explains his mistake. What is Dr. Tazi's legal situation?
options: He is compliant, display in the waiting room is sufficient
He is in violation, the receipt number must appear in all notices
He is compliant, paper files do not require a number
He is in violation, because he cannot use paper
questions.explanation: Dr. Chamssi explains: 'The CNDP receipt number must be integrated into all information notices and forms.' Dr. Tazi: 'I will correct my notices.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi uses cloud-based management software hosted abroad. Dr. Tazi keeps his files at the practice. According to Articles 43 and 44 of Law 09-08, what additional step must Dr. Chamssi take?
options: None, the cloud is considered local storage
A request for data transfer abroad to the CNDP
Only a simplified declaration
A notification to the Ministry of Health
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Cloud hosting abroad involves a transfer of data outside Morocco. You must make a transfer request to the CNDP.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will make this request.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has made a CNDP declaration for his software. Dr. Tazi has made a declaration for his paper files. According to Article 19, what is the deadline for issuing the receipt?
options: 24 hours for digital, 8 days for paper
8 days for digital, 24 hours for paper
24 hours for both
8 days for both
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Article 19 provides that the CNDP issues the receipt within 24 hours, regardless of the medium.' Dr. Chamssi: 'We are therefore treated the same way.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has installed a digital video surveillance camera. Dr. Tazi simply has a mirror without a camera. According to CNDP deliberation No. 350-2013, what regime applies to Dr. Chamssi?
options: A mandatory prior authorization
A simplified declaration in accordance with the deliberation
No declaration, video surveillance is free
A normal declaration with an 8-day deadline
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Video surveillance falls under the simplified declaration regime (form F214) in accordance with deliberation No. 350-2013.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will make the simplified declaration.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi uses a digital scanner to archive his documents. Dr. Tazi still uses paper. Regarding probative value, what is Dr. Chamssi's situation?
options: His documents have no legal value
His documents have the same probative force as paper if kept with integrity
His documents have higher value than paper
He must keep both versions
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The electronic document has the same probative force as paper, provided its integrity is guaranteed.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will guarantee the integrity of my archives.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has digitized all his invoices. Dr. Tazi still keeps his paper invoices. What is the legal retention period for both?
options: 5 years for digital, 10 years for paper
10 years for both, regardless of the medium
6 years for both
3 years for digital, 6 years for paper
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The retention period for accounting documents is 10 years, regardless of the medium.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will keep my digital invoices for 10 years.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has installed CRM software. Dr. Tazi uses a paper appointment book. According to Law 09-08, what is the common obligation for both?
options: Keep a register of processing, regardless of the medium
Only Dr. Chamssi must keep a register
Only Dr. Tazi must keep a register
Neither has any obligation
questions.explanation: Dr. Chamssi explains: 'Law 09-08 requires keeping a register of processing, regardless of the medium.' Dr. Tazi: 'I will create a register for my paper files.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has made a request for prior authorization for his health data. Dr. Tazi believes that his paper files are exempt. According to Article 21, who is right?
options: Dr. Tazi is right: paper health data is exempt
Dr. Chamssi is right: health data requires authorization, regardless of the medium
Dr. Chamssi is wrong: digital health data falls under a simple declaration
Dr. Tazi is right: only digital storage is regulated
questions.explanation: Dr. Chamssi explains: 'Article 21 considers health data as sensitive, regardless of the medium. Prior authorization is mandatory.' Dr. Tazi: 'I will make my authorization request.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi suffered data loss due to a failure. Dr. Tazi saw his paper files destroyed by a fire. What is the common point between their situations?
options: The obligation to notify the loss to the CNDP
The obligation to notify the breach to the CNSS
The obligation to inform the patients concerned in the event of a breach
The obligation to make a declaration to the Order
questions.explanation: Dr. Chamssi explains: 'In the event of a data breach, we must inform the persons concerned, regardless of the medium.' Dr. Tazi: 'I will inform my patients of the loss of their files.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has made a CNDP declaration for his SaaS software. Dr. Tazi has made a declaration for his paper files. What is the fundamental difference in Dr. Chamssi's responsibility?
options: Dr. Chamssi is not responsible, the host is
Dr. Chamssi has an obligation to subcontract with security clauses
Dr. Tazi has more responsibilities
There is no difference in responsibility
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'By using a subcontractor, you must conclude a contract with clauses guaranteeing data security.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will check my contract with the host.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has digitized his files and makes them remotely accessible via a portal. Dr. Tazi keeps the traditional system. According to Article 5, must the information notices be different?
options: Yes, Dr. Chamssi must provide more detailed notices for the portal
No, the notices must be the same regardless of the medium
Yes, only Dr. Tazi must inform his patients
No, the law does not provide for an information obligation
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The portal collects additional data, you must inform your patients of these new processing operations.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will adapt my information notices.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi uses electronic signatures for his prescriptions. Dr. Tazi uses handwritten signatures. According to archiving standards, what advantage does the electronic signature offer?
options: No advantage, the two signatures have the same value
The electronic signature guarantees integrity and authenticity
The electronic signature exempts from keeping documents
The electronic signature is less reliable
questions.explanation: Dr. Chamssi explains: 'The electronic signature guarantees the integrity and authenticity of the document, with a timestamp and digital fingerprint.' Dr. Tazi: 'I will consider electronic signatures.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has opted for an EDMS for his archives. Dr. Tazi keeps his archives in cabinets. What is the advantage of Dr. Chamssi's system?
options: Storage is less expensive but searching is longer
Search is faster and access is easier, but security requirements are reinforced
There is no advantage
The paper system is more reliable
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'EDMS allows quick search but imposes reinforced security requirements.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will reinforce the security of my EDMS.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has made a CNDP declaration. Dr. Tazi has made a declaration for his paper files. What must imperatively appear in the information notices of both?
options: The telephone number of the President of the Order
The CNDP receipt number and the rights of access, rectification, and objection
The color of the folders used
The exact model of the software used
questions.explanation: Dr. Chamssi explains: 'The notices must include the CNDP receipt number, the purposes, and the rights of access, rectification, and objection.' Dr. Tazi: 'I will add these notices to my documents.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has hosted his data with a certified HDS provider. Dr. Tazi does not need a provider. What does HDS certification bring to Dr. Chamssi?
options: A tax reduction
A guarantee of security and compliance with health data requirements
An exemption from CNDP declaration
A dispensation from subcontracting
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'HDS certification guarantees that the provider respects security requirements specific to health data.' Dr. Chamssi: 'That's reassuring for my patients.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has integrated his software with an online appointment booking platform. Dr. Tazi uses the telephone. According to the CNDP deliberation on cookies, what additional obligation does Dr. Chamssi have?
options: None
Collect the prior consent of visitors for the cookies on his site
Declare the tool to the Order of Dentists
Install an antivirus on his site
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Using cookies on your online appointment site requires collecting prior consent from visitors.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will set up a consent banner.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has set up an automatic backup system. Dr. Tazi has a copy of his files at a colleague's. Are the two approaches equivalent?
options: Yes, both approaches are valid
No, Dr. Chamssi's backup must comply with security standards
Yes, because both are backups
No, the paper copy at a colleague's is prohibited
questions.explanation: Dr. Chamssi explains: 'Backups are subject to the same security requirements as the main processing.' Dr. Tazi: 'I will secure my backup at my colleague's.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has digitized files for an indefinite period. Dr. Tazi keeps them without limit. According to Article 6, what is their obligation?
options: Keep the data indefinitely
Set a limited and proportionate retention period
No retention period
Destroy the files after 3 years
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The principle of proportionality requires not keeping data beyond the necessary time.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will set a retention period.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has made a CNDP declaration. Dr. Tazi has made a request for prior authorization. What is the difference between the two procedures?
options: No difference
The declaration is for non-sensitive data, the authorization for sensitive data
The declaration only concerns digital data
Authorization is faster
questions.explanation: Dr. Chamssi explains: 'The declaration is the default regime. Authorization is required for sensitive data like health data.' Dr. Tazi: 'I understand better now.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has made a CNDP declaration. Dr. Tazi must obtain prior authorization. What is the risk for Dr. Tazi if he implements his processing without authorization?
options: No risk
A fine of 10,000 to 100,000 DH and/or prison sentences
A simple injunction
A ban on practicing
questions.explanation: Dr. Chamssi explains: 'Implementing processing subject to authorization without having obtained it exposes you to the fine provided for in Article 52.' Dr. Tazi: 'I will make my authorization request before starting.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has installed management software. Dr. Tazi still uses filing cabinets. According to Law 09-08, can Dr. Chamssi use the data for anonymized statistical studies?
options: Yes, because the data is anonymized
Yes, if he declares it to the CNDP
No, medical data cannot be used
No, the statistical study requires authorization
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Law 09-08 does not apply to anonymized data, because it no longer allows identification of individuals.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will anonymize the data for my statistics.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi wishes to use facial recognition for access to his practice. Dr. Tazi uses physical keys. According to CNDP deliberation D-108-EUS/2020, must Dr. Chamssi obtain prior authorization?
options: No, facial recognition is free
Yes, specific prior authorization is required
Yes, but only for research
No, he can install this system freely
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The use of facial recognition is considered sensitive processing and requires prior authorization from the CNDP.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will make the authorization request.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi, after bringing his practice into compliance with Dr. Tazi, receives his congratulations. What is the next step for Dr. Chamssi?
options: Become an expert in dental data protection
Retire
Change specialty
Forget good practices
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Mastery of data protection is a valuable skill. Becoming an expert is the next step.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will train in data protection.'
